 Mumbai, November 16 : Petrol and diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Monday, November 16. Petrol was retailing at Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi and Rs 111.21 in Mumbai, while diesel prices stood at Rs 95.20 and Rs 97.83 per litre, respectively.    
 Oil prices declined on Monday, November 16, as expectations of a global supply surplus weighed on crude benchmarks, with recovering shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and easing geopolitical concerns adding to bearish sentiment. Brent crude futures fell 1% to $94 . 86 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined 0.7% to $87 . 9 per barrel.   
 The decline comes after crude oil prices ended lower on Friday, extending losses following a sharp correction in the previous week. Brent and WTI had shed 16% and 13%, respectively, in the week before that, as markets reassessed supply risks linked to the US-Israeli war against Iran and the outlook for global oil availability.   
 The International Energy Agency (IEA) said the global oil market is expected to return to a supply surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026, reversing its earlier forecast of a deficit. The agency estimates that global oil supply will average 105 million barrels per day during the quarter, exceeding projected demand by 1.7 million barrels per day.   
 The change in outlook reflects a faster-than-expected recovery in crude exports from the Middle East, even as shipping risks persist. Shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global energy supplies, have nearly recovered to levels seen before the conflict, easing concerns about prolonged supply disruptions.   
 The IEA also said that 71 million barrels from emergency oil reserves pledged by member countries would become available by the end of February, including 15 million barrels of diesel. The additional supply is expected to further ease market tightness.   
 Prices also came under pressure after US President Donald Trump extended a 90-day waiver of the Jones Act, which requires cargo transported between American ports to be carried on US-flagged vessels. The extension allows foreign-flagged ships to transport crude oil, gasoline and diesel more easily between domestic ports, increasing the availability of vessels for fuel shipments.   
 However, elevated shipping costs could limit the extent of the decline in crude prices. Risks associated with tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz and vessels being tied up in transferring oil between ships continue to constrain available shipping capacity, providing some support to prices.   
 Geopolitical risks have also not disappeared entirely. Iranian state media reported that an oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday night. Reuters said it could not independently verify the report.   
 The oil market is therefore witnessing a shift in sentiment, with traders increasingly focusing on the possibility of excess supply rather than the shortages that dominated concerns during the conflict. However, developments around Middle Eastern shipping routes remain an important source of uncertainty for crude prices.   
 Check the latest city-wise petrol and diesel rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and other cities.   
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Monday, November 16, with no revision recorded in any of the metro cities or state capitals listed. In New Delhi, petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre, while the rate in Mumbai stood at Rs 111.21 per litre.   
 Among the four major metro cities, Kolkata had the highest petrol price at Rs 113.51 per litre, followed by Mumbai at Rs 111.21 and Chennai at Rs 107.76. Bengaluru recorded a price of Rs 111.68 per litre.   
 Among other cities, Hyderabad continued to have the highest rate at Rs 116.15 per litre, followed by Thiruvananthapuram at Rs 115.49, Jaipur at Rs 113.19 and Patna at Rs 113.37. Petrol was priced at Rs 108.97 per litre in Bhubaneswar.   
 In the National Capital Region, petrol retailed at Rs 102.97 per litre in Gurgaon and Rs 101.96 in Noida, compared with Rs 102.12 in Delhi. Chandigarh recorded the lowest price among the listed cities at Rs 101.54 per litre, while Lucknow’s rate stood at Rs 101.89. All prices remained unchanged from the previous revision. 
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Monday, November 16, with oil marketing companies keeping retail rates steady. In New Delhi, diesel was priced at Rs 95.20 per litre, while the rate in Mumbai stood at Rs 97.83 per litre.   
 Among the four major metro cities, Kolkata recorded the highest diesel price at Rs 99.82 per litre, followed by Bengaluru at Rs 99.56 and Chennai at Rs 99.55. Diesel was cheapest among these metros in Delhi at Rs 95.20 per litre.   
 Among other cities, Thiruvananthapuram recorded the highest diesel price at Rs 104.40 per litre, closely followed by Hyderabad at Rs 104.23. Diesel retailed at Rs 100.68 per litre in Bhubaneswar, Rs 99.36 in Patna and Rs 98.25 in Jaipur.   
 In the National Capital Region, diesel was priced at Rs 95.64 per litre in Gurgaon and Rs 95.44 in Noida, compared with Rs 95.20 in Delhi. Chandigarh recorded the lowest diesel price among all listed cities at Rs 89.47 per litre, while Lucknow’s rate stood at Rs 95.36. No city recorded a change in diesel prices.
